standard.title: Deliver elaborated spoken presentations
standard.description: Plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations that include relevant, elaborated ideas, sequencing ideas and using complex sentences, specialist and technical vocabulary, pitch, tone, pace, volume, and visual and digital features
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan, create, rehearse and deliver structured oral and/or multimodal presentations of arguments and recounts (AC9E4LY07). They have not yet applied a full range of vocal features — pitch, tone, pace, volume — as deliberate presentational tools, or integrated digital features into multimodal presentations.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations that elaborate ideas with relevant detail, sequence ideas logically using complex sentences and specialist vocabulary, and apply pitch, tone, pace and volume deliberately to support audience understanding and engagement.

nodes.label: Planning: sequencing and elaborating ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a spoken or multimodal presentation that sequences ideas logically and includes relevant, elaborated supporting detail for each main point.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a presentation that sequences at least three main ideas logically and includes at least one piece of elaborating detail (supporting evidence, example, or explanation) for each idea.
nodes.typical_width: Plan a report or presentation on a topic with a logical idea sequence, supporting detail for each idea, and consideration of how graphics, sound or visuals can enhance audience understanding. Apply a planning strategy that distinguishes main ideas from supporting elaborations.
wider: Compare planning approaches for presentations with different purposes (report, argument, narrative) — examining how purpose shapes how ideas are sequenced and what counts as relevant elaboration
Plan a multimodal presentation that distributes ideas across spoken and visual channels — deciding which ideas are best presented through speech and which through visual support
success_criteria: Produces a plan that sequences main ideas logically and includes at least one elaborating detail per idea.
The plan distinguishes between main ideas and supporting elaborations.

nodes.label: Language choices for spoken presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use complex sentences and specialist vocabulary in a spoken presentation, making choices appropriate to the presentation's purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: In a rehearsed presentation, use at least two complex sentences and at least two specialist vocabulary items, and explain how each choice serves the presentation's purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Use complex sentence structures and specialist vocabulary appropriate to topic and audience in a spoken presentation. Apply new learning through vocabulary choices that reflect the presentation's subject knowledge. Choose vocabulary and sentence structures that are appropriate for formal presentation register.
wider: Compare a transcript of a spoken presentation with its written equivalent — examining how the same ideas are packaged differently in spoken and written language, and what complex sentences sound like versus how they read
Reflect on how new learning during research has been incorporated into vocabulary choices in the presentation — developing metacognitive awareness of how subject knowledge shapes language choices
success_criteria: Uses at least two complex sentences in the presentation — the complexity is audible in delivery, not just in the written plan.
Applies specialist vocabulary accurately and in context — not just appended as labels.

nodes.label: Vocal features for engagement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply pitch, tone, pace and volume deliberately in a presentation to support audience understanding and engagement, and explain the effect of those choices.
nodes.minimum_width: In a rehearsed presentation, demonstrate deliberate variation in at least two vocal features (pitch, tone, pace, or volume) and explain what each variation was intended to achieve.
nodes.typical_width: Experiment with vocal features — tone, volume, pitch and pace — in formal presentations, recognising the effects these have on audience understanding and engagement. Apply deliberate vocal variation at key points: slowing for emphasis, raising volume for impact, varying tone for distinction between ideas.
wider: Record and review a presentation, analysing how vocal feature choices actually landed versus the intended effect — using the recording as feedback data for refinement
Compare how vocal feature conventions differ across presentation contexts (classroom report, debate, storytelling, formal speech) and discuss how context shapes appropriate vocal choices

response_modes.reason: Students commonly treat vocal features as performance decoration rather than as communication tools. Experimenting with vocal variations across different presentation contexts — and seeing the audience effects — helps students understand that pitch, pace, tone and volume are meaning-making choices, not performance polish.

success_criteria: Demonstrates at least two deliberate vocal feature variations in a presentation.
Can explain what each vocal choice was intended to achieve for the audience — the choice is deliberate, not accidental.

nodes.label: Integrating visual and digital features
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan and use visual and digital features in a multimodal presentation to support and extend the spoken content, explaining how each feature contributes to audience understanding.
nodes.minimum_width: Include at least two visual or digital features in a presentation and explain how each contributes to the audience's understanding of the ideas presented.
nodes.typical_width: Plan and deliver a multimodal presentation that integrates spoken content with visual and digital features — graphics, sound, visuals — selected to enhance audience engagement and understanding. Explain how the visual/digital and spoken channels work together, not independently.
wider: Compare how visual and digital features function differently in a live presentation versus a recorded or asynchronous presentation — discussing how audience and delivery context shape feature choices
Evaluate a peer's use of visual/digital features in a presentation and provide feedback on whether each feature enhanced or distracted from the spoken content

response_modes.reason: This node requires students to integrate planning (node 1), language choice (node 2), and vocal delivery (node 3) with visual/digital feature selection into a complete multimodal presentation — the full delivery demand of the descriptor.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of visual and digital features available — graphics, audio, video, slide design, physical demonstration — across presentation contexts is genuinely rich. Advancing students can develop a principled framework for multimodal design that connects feature selection to audience and purpose.
success_criteria: Includes at least two visual or digital features and can explain how each contributes to audience understanding.
The visual/digital features support the spoken content — they are not just slides with repeated text.
